title: Task-Driven Subspace Decomposition for Knowledge Sharing and Isolation in LoRA-based Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2603.00191v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Continual Learning (CL) requires models to sequentially adapt to new tasks without forgetting old knowledge. Recently, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a representative Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) method, has gained increasing attention in CL. Several LoRA-based CL methods reduce interference across tasks by separating their update spaces, typically building the new space from the estimated null space of past tasks. However, they (i) overlook task-shared directions, which suppresses knowledge transfer, and (ii) fail to capture truly effective task-specific directions since these ``null bases" of old tasks can remain nearly inactive for new task under correlated tasks. translated_title: 基于LoRA的持续学习中面向知识共享与隔离的任务驱动子空间分解
translated_abstract: 持续学习（CL）要求模型在不遗忘旧知识的前提下依次适应新任务。近来，低秩适配作为参数高效微调（PEFT）的代表性方法，在持续学习领域受到越来越多的关注。一些基于LoRA的持续学习方法通过分离各任务的更新空间来减少任务间的干扰，通常是利用过去任务估计的零空间来构建新的更新空间。然而，这些方法（i）忽略了任务共享的方向，从而抑制了知识迁移；（ii）无法捕捉真正有效的任务特定方向，因为在任务相关的情形下，旧任务的“零空间基”对新任务而言可能几乎不活跃。为解决这一问题，我们从投影能量的视角研究了LoRA的学习能力，并提出了低秩分解与适配方法（LoDA）。该方法通过执行任务驱动的分解，求解两个能量（优化问题），从而构建出通用的以及真正任务特定的LoRA子空间。
tldr: 提出LoDA方法，从投影能量视角出发进行任务驱动的低秩子空间分解，在基于LoRA的持续学习中同时实现跨任务知识共享与真正有效的任务特定隔离。
en_tdlr: Proposes LoDA, which performs task-driven low-rank subspace decomposition from a projection energy perspective to achieve both knowledge sharing and truly effective task-specific isolation in LoRA-based continual learning.
